notes: MANUALLY CREATED RECORD. Ellen M Larkin's mother: ELLEN McALONE — maiden name from both children's GRO registrations, forename from the 1911 census (wife, 46) AND independently from the Dec Q 1894 Whitehaven marriage index (10b/1026), the only Larkin x McAlone marriage ever registered in England & Wales. Daughter Ellen was named for her.

CHILDREN (the 1894 marriage's textbook sequence in Whitehaven registrations): William (Sep Q 1895), Mary Ann (Mar Q 1897, prob. d. 1924 aged 27), Albert Ernest (Mar Q 1898), Catherine (Dec Q 1899, died in infancy), Hugh (b. 4 Dec 1900, d. Whitehaven Jun Q 1972), Samuel (28 Feb 1903 - 1973, M0002), Ellen (Nov 1906, I182195857362). GRO MMN spot-checks on the older children should all read McALONE.

ORIGIN: the Whitehaven McAlones are an Irvinestown (Co. Fermanagh/Tyrone) family — the exact-spelling surname clusters there almost exclusively in Irish civil records. Her birth: either the only E&W Ellen McAlone birth (Sep Q 1874, Whitehaven 10b/615 — but that makes her 36 in 1911, vs the census's 46) or, more consistent with the census, Irish-born ~1865 (Irvinestown-area, pre-registration or as McAloon). Probable father: Patrick McAlone (d. Whitehaven Mar Q 1906, aged 52) or the 1865 Whitehaven groom. The 1894 marriage certificate names her father — the cheap decisive record.

DEATH — SHE PROBABLY SURVIVED TO 1942: no female Larkin death of the right profile anywhere in Cumberland 1907-1941; the only candidate is Ellen Larkin, died Jun Q 1942, Whitehaven 10b/1017, aged 77 (b. ~1865 — matching the census age). So she was most likely ALIVE when 14-year-old Ellen emigrated alone in 1921 — the solo crossing needs another explanation (father's death, poverty, being sent to Maine relatives), and mother and daughter apparently never lived on the same continent again.
NOT her: 'Mary Ellen Larkin d. Mar Q 1906 aged 42' is Simon Larkin's wife née DORAN (m. Sep Q 1888, 10b/795) — a different Whitehaven Larkin household, now fully accounted for.
